candidate_evidence_reviews.name: OVHIPEC-1
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: FIGO stage III; interval cytoreductive surgery after neoadjuvant platinum-taxane chemotherapy
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy in Ovarian Cancer

followups.title: Cytoreductive surgery with or without hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy in patients with advanced ovarian cancer (OVHIPEC-1): final survival analysis of a randomised, controlled, phase 3 trial

evidence.design: Multicentre, open-label, phase III randomized trial; 245 randomized (surgery n=123; surgery+HIPEC n=122).
evidence.population: Stage III epithelial ovarian cancer with at least stable disease after three cycles of carboplatin (AUC 5–6) plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m²; interval surgery feasible for complete or optimal cytoreduction.
evidence.intervention: Interval cytoreductive surgery plus cisplatin HIPEC 100 mg/m²; postoperative carboplatin/paclitaxel for three further cycles.
evidence.comparator: Interval cytoreductive surgery without HIPEC; same postoperative chemotherapy.
evidence.followup: Final survival analysis; median follow-up approximately 10.1 years.
evidence.efficacy: Final analysis: median recurrence-free survival 14.3 vs 10.7 months (HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48–0.83); median OS 44.9 vs 33.3 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.53–0.92). Original primary report: grade 3–4 adverse events 27% with HIPEC vs 25% without.
evidence.nnt: Not applicable: median RFS/OS and HRs alone are not valid NNT inputs; no verified common fixed-time absolute survival rates used.

missing_evidence: Final analysis table-level denominators and exact p values rechecked against full paper/supplement
HIPEC perfusion temperature, duration and sodium-thiosulfate protocol verified from protocol/supplement
Complete grade 3–5 toxicity and perioperative morbidity tables
Patient-reported QoL and treatment-burden data
Current guideline mapping

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: PRIMA/ENGOT-OV26/GOG-3012
candidate_evidence_reviews.site: Advanced epithelial ovarian/fallopian tube/primary peritoneal cancer
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: Newly diagnosed stage III–IV; maintenance after response to first-line platinum chemotherapy
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Niraparib in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Advanced Ovarian Cancer

followups.title: Final overall survival and long-term safety results from the PRIMA/ENGOT-OV26/GOG-3012 trial

evidence.design: Randomized, double-blind, phase III, placebo-controlled; 733 randomized 2:1 (niraparib n=487; placebo n=246).
evidence.population: Newly diagnosed stage III–IV high-grade serous/endometrioid ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal carcinoma; complete/partial response after 6–9 cycles of first-line platinum chemotherapy; HRD defined by deleterious BRCA mutation and/or myChoice GIS ≥42.
evidence.intervention: Oral niraparib once daily for up to 36 months or progression; initial 300 mg daily, amended individualized starting dose 200 mg if baseline weight <77 kg and/or platelets <150,000/mm³.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival hierarchically tested in HRD and overall populations.
evidence.efficacy: HRD median PFS 21.9 vs 10.4 months (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59; p<0.001); overall median PFS 13.8 vs 8.2 months (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50–0.76; p<0.001). Final OS analysis: HR 1.01 (95% CI 0.84–1.23; p=0.8834); 5-year PFS 22% vs 12% overall and 35% vs 16% in HRD.
evidence.safety: Grade ≥3 anemia 31.0%, thrombocytopenia 28.7%, neutropenia 12.8%; thrombocytopenia led to discontinuation in 4.3%; primary publication reports no decrement in patient-reported quality of life. Long-term MDS/AML approximately 2.3% vs 1.6%.
evidence.nnt: Landmark PFS: 5-year overall-population difference 10 percentage points (22−12), NNT 10; HRD difference 19 points (35−16), NNT 6. These are Kaplan–Meier landmark estimates, not crude event-count NNTs.

missing_evidence: Full grade 4–5 and serious adverse-event table extraction
Dose intensity, dose reductions/interruptions and treatment exposure by arm
Complete PRO/QoL domain scores and missing-data handling
Final OS subgroup/stratification table-level verification
Current guideline mapping

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: ALPINE
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: Relapsed/refractory after at least one prior therapy
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Zanubrutinib or Ibrutinib in Relapsed or Refractory Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia

followups.title: Final comparative analysis of zanubrutinib versus ibrutinib in patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia

evidence.design: Open-label, randomized phase III; 652 patients randomized 1:1.
evidence.population: Relapsed/refractory CLL/SLL after at least one prior systemic therapy.
evidence.intervention: Zanubrutinib 160 mg orally twice daily, continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
evidence.comparator: Ibrutinib 420 mg orally once daily, continuous until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Overall response rate; PFS a key secondary endpoint.
evidence.efficacy: At the primary analysis, 24-month PFS 78.4% vs 65.9%; PFS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49–0.86; p=0.002). Final comparative analysis at approximately 42.5 months retained a PFS advantage (HR approximately 0.68).
evidence.nnt: 24-month PFS landmark difference 12.5 percentage points; NNT 8 (ceil[1/0.125]).

missing_evidence: Exact final-analysis denominators, confidence interval and p value re-extraction from full Blood article/supplement
Grade 3–5 adverse-event table and cardiac/bleeding/infection breakdown
Treatment discontinuation and exposure by arm
Patient-reported outcomes/QoL

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: MAIA
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Daratumumab plus Lenalidomide and Dexamethasone for Untreated Myeloma

followups.title: Final overall survival analysis of the MAIA study

evidence.design: Open-label randomized phase III; 737 transplant-ineligible patients.
evidence.population: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma not eligible for autologous stem-cell transplantation.
evidence.intervention: Daratumumab plus lenalidomide and dexamethasone (D-Rd); daratumumab IV 16 mg/kg weekly cycles 1–2, every 2 weeks cycles 3–6, then every 4 weeks; lenalidomide 25 mg days 1–21 of 28-day cycles; dexamethasone weekly.
evidence.comparator: Lenalidomide plus dexamethasone (Rd) on the same 28-day cycle.
evidence.efficacy: Final OS analysis at median follow-up 89.3 months: median OS 90.3 vs 64.1 months (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.55–0.82); 7-year OS 53.1% vs 39.3%.
evidence.safety: The 2026 final OS report did not collect updated nonfatal AE data; original primary publication safety must be used and explicitly labelled as earlier follow-up.
evidence.nnt: 7-year OS landmark difference 13.8 percentage points; NNT 8 (ceil[1/0.138]).

missing_evidence: Re-extract original primary publication grade 3–5 AE, infections, cytopenias and discontinuations
Complete patient-reported QoL and treatment-burden data
Verify final OS analysis publication date versus issue date; it was electronically published 2026-08-24 and is not within the preceding month for ToD
Dose modifications/exposure and stratification details

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: PERSEUS
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Daratumumab, Bortezomib, Lenalidomide, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma

evidence.design: Open-label randomized phase III; 709 transplant-eligible patients.
evidence.population: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma eligible for autologous stem-cell transplantation.
evidence.intervention: Daratumumab plus bortezomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (D-VRd), followed by autologous transplantation, consolidation and daratumumab/lenalidomide maintenance.
evidence.comparator: VRd induction, autologous transplantation, consolidation and lenalidomide maintenance.
evidence.efficacy: At median follow-up 47.5 months, 48-month PFS 84.3% vs 67.7%; HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.30–0.59; p<0.001).
evidence.safety: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 62.1% vs 51.0%; thrombocytopenia 29.1% vs 17.3%; serious adverse events 57.0% vs 49.3%.
evidence.nnt: 48-month PFS landmark difference 16.6 percentage points; NNT 7 (ceil[1/0.166]).

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: CARTITUDE-4
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: Lenalidomide-refractory relapsed/refractory disease after 1–3 prior lines
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Cilta-cel or Standard Care in Lenalidomide-Refractory Multiple Myeloma

evidence.design: Open-label randomized phase III; 419 patients (cilta-cel n=208; standard care n=211).
evidence.population: Lenalidomide-refractory myeloma after 1–3 prior lines including a proteasome inhibitor and an immunomodulatory drug.
evidence.intervention: Leukapheresis followed by ciltacabtagene autoleucel after lymphodepletion; bridging therapy permitted while product manufactured.
evidence.comparator: Physician-choice standard care: pomalidomide/bortezomib/dexamethasone or daratumumab/pomalidomide/dexamethasone.
evidence.efficacy: At median follow-up 15.9 months, median PFS not reached vs 11.8 months; HR 0.26 (95% CI 0.18–0.38; p<0.001). 12-month PFS 75.9% vs 48.6%.
evidence.safety: Cytokine-release syndrome 76.1% (grade 3–4 1.1%); ICANS 4.5% (grade 1–2); cranial nerve palsy 9.1%; peripheral neuropathy 2.8%.
evidence.nnt: 12-month PFS landmark difference 27.3 percentage points; NNT 4 (ceil[1/0.273]).

Updated grade 3–5 AE and treatment-related mortality from mature follow-up
Full patient-reported outcomes and QoL

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: DREAMM-7
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: Relapsed/refractory after at least one prior line
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Belantamab Mafodotin, Bortezomib, and Dexamethasone for Multiple Myeloma

evidence.design: Open-label randomized phase III; 494 patients (BVd n=243; DVd n=251).
evidence.population: Relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma after at least one prior line.
evidence.intervention: Belantamab mafodotin plus bortezomib and dexamethasone (BVd).
evidence.efficacy: At median follow-up 28.2 months, median PFS 36.6 vs 13.4 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.31–0.53; p<0.001); 18-month OS 84% vs 73%; complete response or better plus MRD-negative 25% vs 10%.
evidence.safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events 95% vs 78%; ocular events 79% vs 29%, usually managed with dose modifications; worsening visual acuity mostly resolved.
evidence.nnt: 18-month OS landmark difference 11 percentage points; NNT 10 (ceil[1/0.11]).

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: AEGEAN
candidate_evidence_reviews.setting: Perioperative; neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy followed by adjuvant immunotherapy
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Perioperative Durvalumab for Resectable Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer

followups.title: Long-term follow-up of perioperative durvalumab in resectable NSCLC (AEGEAN)

evidence.design: Double-blind randomized phase III; 802 patients (durvalumab n=400; placebo n=402).
evidence.population: Previously untreated resectable stage II–IIIB (N2) NSCLC; EGFR/ALK-altered patients excluded from the primary efficacy population by protocol amendment.
evidence.intervention: Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 3 weeks with four cycles of platinum-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy, surgery, then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks for 12 cycles.
evidence.comparator: Placebo with the same neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy, surgery and adjuvant placebo schedule.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Event-free survival and pathological complete response.
evidence.efficacy: Primary analysis EFS HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.53–0.88; p=0.004); pCR 17.2% vs 4.3%. 2026 follow-up at median 25.9 months: EFS HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.55–0.88); DFS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.47–0.92); OS HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.70–1.14).
evidence.safety: Grade 3–4 adverse events during neoadjuvant treatment approximately 42.4% vs 43.2%; adjuvant grade 3–4 AEs 15.4% vs 10.6% in the follow-up report.
evidence.nnt: pCR absolute difference 12.9 percentage points (17.2−4.3); NNT 8 for one additional pCR.

missing_evidence: Exact chemotherapy backbone by histology and renal/neuropathy eligibility
Detailed surgical completion and postoperative treatment exposure
Full grade 3–5 AE table and treatment discontinuations
QoL/PRO and patient-reported symptoms
Current NCCN perioperative recommendation mapping

candidate_evidence_reviews.name: IMpower010
candidate_evidence_reviews.primary_title: Adjuvant atezolizumab after adjuvant chemotherapy in resected stage IB–IIIA non-small-cell lung cancer (IMpower010): a randomised, multicentre, open-label, phase 3 trial

followups.title: Five-year follow-up of adjuvant atezolizumab in resected NSCLC (IMpower010)

evidence.design: Open-label randomized phase III; 1005 patients in the intention-to-treat population.
evidence.population: Completely resected stage IB (tumour ≥4 cm)–IIIA NSCLC after cisplatin-based adjuvant chemotherapy.
evidence.intervention: Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks for 16 cycles (approximately one year).
evidence.comparator: Best supportive care/observation after adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed disease-free survival in stage II–IIIA tumours with PD-L1 expression ≥1%.
evidence.efficacy: At median follow-up 32 months, DFS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.50–0.88; p=0.0039) in stage II–IIIA PD-L1 ≥1%; stage II–IIIA overall HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.64–0.96; p=0.020). Five-year follow-up: ITT DFS HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.71–1.01; p=0.07); stage II–IIIA PD-L1 ≥1% HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55–0.91); ITT OS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.78–1.22).
evidence.safety: Full grade 3–5 safety table not extracted in this review.
evidence.nnt: Not applicable from HR-only long-term results; no verified common fixed-time absolute DFS/OS rates used.

Grade 3–5 AE, immune-mediated toxicity and discontinuation tables
